## What's (computationally) "Reproducible"?

- Someone *else* (or *you*?)...
- can replicate your results given the
  - original data
  - documentation
  - any necessary code
- (but make it *easy*)
- Conflicting value: data privacy

---

# Our Stories

---
## Why Quarto (or Rmarkdown)?

- Combine code *and* text
- Generate reports, slides, websites, ebooks...
- Embed/store code without necessarily showing it
- Remember what you did
- Quickly make corrections or add new data
- ...

---
## What about Git/GitHub?
### What is it *for* and why might you use it?

.small[
- Store, share, and collaborate on code
- Track changes over time (who, what, when)
  - *and without my-report-final.pdf, my-report-final2.pdf...*
- Ability to revert
- Control over what to add to shared repository, when
- Know who uses and builds on your code
- Easy websites / documents hosted online
- It's *not* for: large files
]

---
class: smaller
## Learn More: Reproducible Research

- [A Beginner's Guide to Conducting Reproducible Research](https://doi.org/10.1002/bes2.1801) (Jesse Alston & Jessica Rick)
- [Open science, reproducibility, and transparency in ecology](https://doi.org/10.1002/eap.1822) (Stephen Powers & Stephanie Hampton)
- [Best Practices for Scientific Computing](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745) and [Good Enough Practices for Scientific Computing](https://swcarpentry.github.io/good-enough-practices-in-scientific-computing/) (Greg Wilson & colleagues) (But seriously...`src` and `bin`?)
- [Pragmatic Reproducible Research](https://doi.org/10.1172/JCI173741) (Luke Rasmussen & colleagues)
- [Reproducibility and Replicability in Science](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547532/) (book @ nih.gov)
- [Eleven strategies for making reproducible research...the norm](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.89736) (Friederike Kohrs & colleagues)
- [...Data and Methods Transparency in Nonprofit Research](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11266-025-00736-0) (René Bekkers & colleagues)
